RoleyX Bond S10 Is a Flagship E-Scooter From a New Chinese Brand – Coming in Hot at $1,200
17 photos
Photo: RoleyX
With each passing day, it seems that there’s a new e-scooter brand popping up and frankly, that’s kind of the case. This time around, we explore one such crew and what they promise to bring to the table.
If you type in “RoleyX” in a Google search bar, the first result you’ll get is “Rolex,” as if this omnipotent search engine has no idea who RoleyX may be. That’s how new this crew is, with the name hitting the scene in mid to late 2026. Currently, they only offer one unit, and that’s what we’re here to explore.
It’s called the Bond S10, and while it may not have anything to do with the film franchise, nor do I know what that S10 stands for, it is this brand’s first e-scooter , or the proverbial flagship, the one that’s meant to showcase what this name is all about.
Photo: RoleyX First and foremost, the S10 is currently up for grabs at no more than $1,200 (€1,100), placing it in the low to middle range in terms of what the market offers, and if I may, it actually brings in some value. There have also been people that said “yes” to this two-wheeler, and for the time being, the S10 does carry a 4.9/5.0-star rating.
One reason why folks are liking this one has a whole lot to do with speed, which is set at a peak of 40 mph (64 kph) out of the box, so plenty of kick to ensure that you can leave the car at home, if only for a few miles each week. Maybe e-scooters are your chosen means of transport.
This top speed is granted by the presence of two motors, with 1,000 W a piece as nominal. However, there is a mention of a peak of 3,200 W on the manufacturer’s website, but it’s not clear if this is per motor, or both together. I’m banking on the latter because 6,400 W would place this one in the hyper scooter range, and it isn’t.
Do note that another section of the product page does mention a peak output of 3,500 W, which is roughly 4.7 hp. Oh, and some riders have reported a top speed that sits higher than 40 mph, so there’s a bit more power than we’re told.
Photo: RoleyX These two motors are also strong enough to help riders up hills with an incline of as much as 35%, which is very good for something in this price range and more than enough pull to ensure some punchy acceleration. The latter stands at a 0-30 mph (0-48 kph) time in under four seconds.
The S10 is also built upon a 52 V ecosystem, accounting for that acceleration. Be sure to have some knowledge of how to ride an e-scooter before playing around with the fastest mode.
One very strong point for the S10 is range, rolling in with a peak of 65 miles (105 km), made possible by a 20 Ah battery mounted into the deck. Clearly, the faster we ride, the less range we can expect, but from my own experience, we can see around 50% of what manufacturers mention zipping around our cities with mixed speed settings.
What I liked about this fresh brand is that they do tell riders what we can expect from rides at full speed; just 16 miles can be accessed if you ride at a constant 40 mph. Once we’re out of juice, it takes up to 10 hours before being able to ride again.
Photo: RoleyX RoleyX does state that their e-scooter carries an IPX6 rating and does show it moving around through puddles and all that, made possible by a patented system and a BMS. Another feature that protects the battery is the frame itself, completed from forged aluminum to resist torsional forces.
Yet, speed means nothing without control, and to ensure that you stay on top of things, literally, a C-arm suspension is called upon, a tried and tested system that countless EV of this style calls upon. Hydraulic shocks are used for damping and rebound, and can handle riders as large as 256 lbs (120 kg).
Allow me to point out that this sort of suspension is one that does allow riders to break away from the tarmac and tackle hardpack roads and even some dirt trails . There are clear limits to e-scooter though, so ride responsibly.
More softness and control are granted by the 10-inch tires with 3.0-inch cross-section. They are pneumatic and tubeless and carry a hybrid tread that will clearly keep you riding fast on tarmac but let us tap into those light off-road settings I mentioned. Rubber compound is also an often-overlooked aspect that contributes to stopping times, so be sure to explore other options out there if the standard ones aren’t to your liking.
Photo: RoleyX In this price range, most brands also integrated hydraulic brakes into the mix and for the S10, this is true too. A pair of oil-activated pistons clamp down on 5.5-inch rotors at the front and rear.
Toss on a display with NFC unlock, ambient lighting in the stem, deck, a headlight ad taillight, and we’re almost done. Almost because the S10 also carries a geometry that’s designed to keep the handlebar as stable as possible at high speeds.
I didn’t make out whether or not the S10 has a steering damper, but RoleyX does showcase a rider rolling around with one hand on the handlebar and the other holding a phone up to his ear. Some sources do mention that there is a steering damper at play too.
From where I'm standing, the S10 is looking pretty good, with real riders claiming the same. Ride safe out there; gear up properly.
